**Goal:** restore an approved computer so another student can use it reliably. This module works independently of later SSH or GitHub lessons.

## Before installing

1. Record the computer's ID, model, RAM, disk capacity, known problems and the operating system currently installed.
2. Obtain the teacher-approved Linux image and bootable USB. Use [Linux Mint](https://linuxmint.com/download.php), preferably its Xfce edition for modest hardware when appropriate. Xubuntu or another approved lightweight system may be substituted. Do not invent a generic Apple boot key sequence: follow the particular model's boot procedure.
3. Use a **live USB session first**. Check keyboard, mouse/pointer visibility, display, Ethernet/Wi-Fi, browser, sound and that the target drive is detected.
4. **Stop at the erase/partition choice.** Show the teacher the exact target disk and confirm that files have been preserved and this device is approved for erasure. Never erase a borrowed or personal device without explicit approval.

## Install and commission

After approval, run the installer and follow the chosen distribution's current instructions. Use teacher-specified language, keyboard, user/account and update settings. At restart, remove installation media when prompted.

### Ready for TAS checklist

- [ ] Machine boots to the installed system after a full restart.
- [ ] Student can log in using the approved account.
- [ ] Display and pointer remain visible; keyboard and mouse work.
- [ ] A web browser opens and the approved network works.
- [ ] Sound, USB ports and storage work where required.
- [ ] Device ID, installed OS/version, missing features and last test date are recorded.
- [ ] Teacher accepts the machine for TAS.

Do not delay handing over a reliable first batch because other computers still have unresolved repairs.

## Student record

Record: assigned device, original fault, installation decisions requiring approval, checks passed/failed, what you fixed and **what I learned**.
